name: ICP Score
blurb: Ranks companies against an ideal-customer profile and shows the arithmetic behind every score. Exclusions are hard filters rather than heavy negative weights, and a missing field says so instead of quietly scoring as a miss.
alt: The ICP Score interface: fifty companies ranked, with one row expanded to show its score breakdown

name: Enrichment Waterfall
blurb: Finds a work email by trying providers in cost order and stopping at the first address that survives verification. Every attempt is recorded: what it returned, why it was kept or thrown out, and what it cost.
alt: The Enrichment Waterfall interface: a run in progress showing each provider stage and its per-attempt cost

name: Signal Scout
blurb: Derives account events by diffing dated observations of the same company, then ages them and ranks accounts by how timely outreach is right now. A feed answers what happened; this answers who to touch today.
alt: The Signal Scout interface: a daily priority board of accounts ranked by decayed signal strength

name: Lead Cleaner
blurb: Record linkage for messy lead and CRM data: tiered matching, constrained clustering, and a field-level receipt for every merge. The same human arriving three times under three spellings collapses into one record you can audit.
alt: The Lead Cleaner review queue: candidate duplicate records with a match threshold slider

name: Persona Mapper
blurb: A company and an offer go in; a buying committee comes out — titles that actually exist at that headcount, in that industry's vocabulary, with an authority ladder tied to deal size. The same offer restructures the committee completely at eight people and at eighteen thousand.
alt: The Persona Mapper interface: a generated buying committee for one company and offer

name: Why Now
blurb: Turns dated company evidence into a "why now" hypothesis where every inferential step is licensed by a declared rule — or the chain visibly breaks at the step that failed. Built because a well-cited non-sequitur is worse than no output at all.
alt: The Why Now interface: an inference chain with each step licensed by a named rule

name: Girth of Nations
blurb: An infinite canvas of ~196 countries that inflate and deflate as strangers drop emoji on them. A country's size is a function of its emoji count, so the map reshapes itself live. No accounts, no posts, six emoji.
alt: The Girth of Nations canvas: country shapes scaled by how many emoji strangers have dropped on them
